newsitem.title: FRANCE: Galliano wows Paris with warehouse gypsy gathering.
newsitem.headline: Galliano wows Paris with warehouse gypsy gathering.

text.p: John Galliano has dazzled the Paris fashion crowd with a spellbinding display of designs staged as a gypsy gathering in an abandoned Paris wine warehouse.

Campfires burned in rusty barrels and ragged clothes hung out to dry as Paris's beau monde soiled their designer shoes tripping on tyres and other rubbish on Thursday to reach the warehouse in a Parisian no-man's land.
Inside, acrobats flipped about and a gypsy band chanted as supermodels sashayed out in tiny dresses of exquisite Chantilly lace or leather motorcycle suits adorned with Indian mirror embroidery.
Then out came the gypsy costumes: fringed Russian shawls stitched into striking bias-cut gowns or a satin belly dancer's ensemble trimmed with astonishingly delicate petit-point.
Each piece was a masterpiece -- from the foamy lace blouses and thigh-high embroidered boots to a magnificent fortune teller's dress with tiers of dark silk edged in ribbons and gold brocade.
It all seemed too magical for real life, but Be Bilzerian, owner of a specialty store in Boston, said Galliano's clothes did go beyond the catwalk.
"Everyone wants to look like a diva for a night," she said. "You don't buy these kinds of clothes, or a Hermes pocketbook if you're worried about the price."
Kalman Ruttenstein of Bloomingdale was more effusive.
"Every couple of years there's a special moment in fashion, and this sure was one. Any weaker word than spectacular would be wrong," he said.
Galliano's theatrics could have come at no better time.

In the front row sat the new owner of his house Bernard Arnault, head of luxury giant LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, who is expected next week to announce Galliano's appointment as designer at Christian Dior, another LVMH asset.
Another mad Briton, Alexander McQueen, is tipped for the position Galliano would be leaving vacant at LVMH sister house Givenchy.
A brief appearance by McQueen at Christian Lacroix's ready-to-wear collection earlier on Thursday was a strong indication he would be Givenchy's new man.
Asked whether he had accepted the Givenchy job, McQueen replied: "I'm afraid you'll have to wait for that."
Earlier, Sonia Rykiel celebrated her 6,000th sweater design, offering a knitwear restrospective spanning the colour spectrum.

The veteran designer, known as the "Queen of Knitwear", then unfurled next summer's knits -- striped middy tube dresses, leopard spotted tank tops over bikini bottoms, lurex draw-string trousers and fishnet tops over tiny shorts which had the photographers roaring with delight.
Finally, she moved on to cotton: striped or plaid jumpsuits, a few magenta trouser suits and jeans with drawstring flies. A colourful, upbeat affair, the show featured over 60 models.
Lolita Lempicka, the queen of separates, sent out bright florals on black, snakeskin chiffons, and vivid colour mixes like fuchsia with orange or magenta with turquoise.

It was everything that trendy teenagers have been wearing on the streets: stretchy flared trousers, viscose knit twinsets and a series of ensembles in chartreuse and flame, the hottest shades from last season's catwalk.
